title: Irelia VS Sivir Aurora: a Grand Final lesson in breaking Aurora tempo
result: EDG Rico1997 defeats TSS SouledOut 2-0 and wins the Sydney Regional Qualifier.

chapters.title: Irelia player view
points: The Irelia plan is not to wait for Dazzling Aurora and answer it head-on. It is to use Adaptatron, information, and movement to break the Aurora player's first clean trigger window.
At 4:06:27, practice the first three beats of Game 1: every spend, move, or open-mana pass should be judged by what it forces the Aurora side to answer first.
At 4:24:33, practice counterspell allocation. Not So Fast should protect the plan that keeps narrowing Aurora's window, not just a random trade.

chapters.title: Sivir Aurora player view
points: Sivir Aurora still has a high ceiling, but the setup turn must clear Adaptatron, open mana, and movement pressure before Dazzling Aurora can be safe.
Game 1 should be reviewed by finding the first turn where the Aurora side stopped advancing its own plan and started answering Irelia's questions.
Game 2 is about dismantling the protection chain before committing to the expensive line, so Elder Dragon or Flurry of Blades does not become the only visible plan.
